info.description: Text to speech with Piper. /v1/speak streams an MP3; /v1/synthesize queues a job that uploads it.
info.title: Piper TTS REST API

post.description:
Streams the MP3 in the response, chunked, without a Content-Length.

Piper writes raw PCM to its stdout and ffmpeg encodes it to MP3 on the fly. The PCM sample rate is read once at startup from the model's `.onnx.json` sidecar.

**Concurrency and cancellation.** `MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default 10) caps the requests handled at once. A slot is held for the whole request: parsing, synthesis, encoding and streaming. When the client disconnects, the piper and ffmpeg processes are killed and awaited, then the slot is freed, so a queued request can start at once. Cancellation is per replica; there is no cross-replica cancellation. Pick a client timeout that allows for synthesis: piper takes about 2 s before the first byte for short inputs, and longer for longer text.

**Performance.** Each request starts a fresh piper process that loads the ONNX voice model (about 61 MB), a fixed cold start of roughly 1.7 to 2 s. The piper CLI has no daemon mode, so this service targets batch and offline narration, not low-latency interactive use. For that, drive piper from Python with a long-lived model.

Queues a job that generates the MP3 and uploads it to a presigned URL. A 202 means queued, not done.

**Callbacks.** Once per attempt the service calls `genUploadUrl` with `{"jobId", "attempt", "contentType": "audio/mpeg"}`. It must reply 200 with `{"uploadUrl": "..."}`, a short-lived presigned PUT URL. Progress goes to `statusCallbackUrl` with an `Idempotency-Key: <jobId>:<attempt>` header.

| Status | Extra fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| queued | | A worker received the job. |
| generating | percent (0-99) | Producing the MP3. |
| uploading | percent (0-99) | Uploading to object storage. |
| completed | fileSizeBytes | Upload succeeded. |
| failed | failedAt, error | Terminal failure, no more retries. |

Percentages are stage-local, approximate and monotonic. Status delivery is best effort: timeouts and non-2xx replies do not stop synthesis. Clients must tolerate duplicate, missing and out-of-order updates.

**Delivery and retries.** RabbitMQ delivery is at least once. A worker crash after the upload and before the acknowledgement can repeat the upload and the callbacks. A retryable failure in generating, getting the upload URL or uploading republishes the job with attempt + 1, up to `SYNTHESIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS`. The delay is the `Retry-After` of a 429 reply (at most one hour), otherwise `SYNTHESIZE_RETRY_DELAY_MS` times the number of the failed attempt. Delayed retries need RabbitMQ 4.4 or newer; older brokers redeliver at once. A job that fails for good gets the failed callback and its message goes to the dead-letter queue.

**Security.** Callback URLs must be HTTPS in production, and URL credentials and fragments are rejected. `SYNTHESIZE_CALLBACK_ALLOWED_HOSTS` restricts the hosts, and the worker refuses non-public addresses unless the host is listed. Presigned URLs are redacted in logs. The optional `Authorization` header is passed through to the callbacks.

**Operations.** The service declares durable exchanges and quorum queues (`synthesize.work`, `synthesize.dlq`) with prefetch 1; give RabbitMQ persistent storage. See the scaling guide in the repository for KEDA and rollout guidance.
